name: Maruti Suzuki India Ltd
about: The Company was established in 1981. A joint venture agreement was signed between the Government of India and Suzuki Motor Corporation (SMC), Japan in 1982. The Company became a subsidiary of SMC in 2002.It is the market leader in passenger vehicle segment in India. In terms of production volume and sales, the Company is now SMC’s largest subsidiary. SMC currently holds 56.28% of its equity stake. The principal activities of the Company are manufacturing, purchase and sale of motor vehicles, components and spare parts.

sections.one_liner: India's passenger-vehicle leader; revenue is up 26-36% but margins have fallen to 8-9%. Can margins recover?
business: Makes passenger vehicles (hatchbacks, sedans, SUVs, MPVs), small commercial vehicles (Super Carry, Eeco Cargo) and finance, insurance and parts services. [AR FY26]
Segment revenue shares not disclosed. Mainly domestic: FY26 volume 2,422,713 units, of which exports were 447,000 (~18%). [Q4FY26 call]
Exports reach ~120 countries; top five are South Africa, Japan, Chile, Saudi Arabia and EU. Claims 49% of India's PV exports. [AR FY26] [Q4FY26 call]
Suzuki is parent: stake 58.53% per AR vs 56.28% per blurb. Suzuki Motor Gujarat amalgamated, so YoY comparability is unclear. [AR FY26] [Numbers]
financial_snapshot: Q2 FY27 (Sep-26): revenue Rs53,356cr (+26.0% YoY); EBITDA Rs4,764cr (-6.3%); PAT Rs2,466cr (-26.4%); OPM 9% vs 12%. [Numbers]
TTM: revenue Rs2,08,192cr, EBITDA Rs20,808cr (OPM ~10.0%), PAT Rs13,451cr, which is below FY26 PAT of Rs14,680cr. [Numbers]
Returns are slipping: ROCE 18.9% vs 22% in FY24-25; ROE 14.3%. Profit is lagging a fast-growing equity base. [Numbers]
Valuation: Rs3.58 lakh cr market cap; 26.6x P/E; ~3.3x book; 1.23% yield. Price Rs11,397 is 34% below high, 4% above low. [Numbers]
trajectory: Revenue CAGR is 21.1% (5y) and 15.7% (3y). The quarterly run-rate stepped up from Rs42k cr (Sep-25) to Rs53k cr (Sep-26). [Numbers]
OPM went 7% (FY22) → 13% (FY24-25) → 12% (FY26) → 8-9% in H1 FY27. The margin expansion cycle has reversed. [Numbers]
Profit growth has stalled. FY26 EBITDA rose +6.5% and PAT +1.2% on +19.9% revenue. H1 FY27 PAT is Rs5,913cr vs Rs7,141cr (-17%). [Numbers]
PAT CAGR of 27.3% over 5y flatters, because the base is the FY21-22 trough. FY26 ROCE of 19% is below the 22% FY24-25 peak. [Numbers]
balance_sheet: Effectively debt-free: borrowings Rs83cr against net worth Rs1,09,002cr (Sep-26); D/E 0.0 throughout. [Numbers]
Supplier funding is shrinking. Working-capital days moved from -50 (FY21) to -29 (FY26); cash conversion cycle from -44 to -19 days. [Numbers]
Inventory days rose from 23 to 31 in FY26 despite a claimed supply shortage and 1.9 lakh pending orders. This needs explaining. [Numbers] [AR FY26]
cash_quality: Profits turn into cash: CFO/PAT is 1.22 over 3 years; FY26 CFO Rs19,100cr vs PAT Rs14,680cr (1.30x). [Numbers]
Capex absorbs a lot of cash. FY23-26 cumulative FCF was Rs24,859cr, only 49% of Rs50,932cr PAT. FY26 capex was ~Rs10,346cr. [Numbers]
The Rs35,000cr Sanand plan plus two 250k lines in FY27 implies capex will stay heavy as margins fall. FCF is at risk. [AR FY26] [Numbers]
narrative_vs_numbers: Management says 'highest ever' FY26 volumes and profit. The numbers show PAT +1.2% on +19.9% revenue, and H1 FY27 PAT -17%. [Q4FY26 call] [Numbers]
Cost headwinds were called 'temporary'. The next two quarters printed 8% and 9% OPM vs a 12% prior run-rate. [Q4FY26 call] [Numbers]
Below-EBITDA erosion: Q2 FY27 PAT fell 26.4% vs EBITDA -6.3%. The Rs750cr bond MTM risk flagged in April may be recurring. [Q4FY26 call] [Numbers]
Capacity and export figures conflict: call targets 4M units vs AR's 3.65M by FY31; AR says '47 lakh' exports vs 447,000 units on call. [Q4FY26 call] [AR FY26]
guidance: FY27 volume growth over 10% vs FY26's 2.42M units. [Q4FY26 call]
Kharkhoda Phase 2 and Hansalpur line 4 operational within FY27, adding 500k units in total. AR targets 2.9M capacity by FY27-end. [Q4FY26 call] [AR FY26]
Medium-term capacity of 4M units/yr. AR says 3.65M by FY31, backed by a Rs35,000cr Sanand investment. [Q4FY26 call] [AR FY26]
10% EBIT margin aspiration by 2030; 'multiple moving parts'. Seven more SUVs through the decade. [Q4FY26 call]
No significant start-up costs from new plants. No Q1 FY27 cost number given. Q3 and Q2 FY26 transcripts unavailable. [Q4FY26 call]

ledger.promised: Cost headwinds from West Asia, commodities and energy are temporary (Q4FY26 call)
ledger.delivered: OPM 8% (Jun-26), 9% (Sep-26) vs 12% a year earlier; EBITDA down ~6-7% YoY both quarters

ledger.promised: No significant start-up costs from Kharkhoda/Gujarat capacity (Q4FY26 call)
ledger.delivered: Q2 EBITDA Rs4,764cr, -6.3% YoY on +26% revenue; cost split not disclosed

ledger.promised: MTM bond hit of Rs750cr partly reversing, ~35% ongoing (Q4FY26 call)
ledger.delivered: PAT -9.1% then -26.4% YoY; Q2 PAT fell 4x faster than EBITDA

ledger.promised: Volume growth over 10% vs FY26 (Q4FY26 call)
ledger.delivered: H1 revenue +36%/+26% YoY; unit volumes not in NUMBERS; full year not reported

ledger.promised: Two 250k-unit lines operational within FY27 (Q4FY26 call)
ledger.delivered: Not disclosed; revenue flat QoQ at Rs52-53k cr in H1 suggests no step-up yet
TTM EBITDA margin ~10.0%; EBIT is lower, implying the target is currently not reached
Approved at Rs140 vs Rs135 prior year; yield 1.23%

bull: Demand exceeds supply: 1.9 lakh pending orders (1.3 lakh small cars); first-time buyers rose from 42% to 51% after GST cut. [Q4FY26 call]
Revenue run-rate is +26-36% YoY. If OPM recovers to 12%, TTM EBITDA of Rs20.8k cr would rise ~20% to ~Rs25k cr. [Numbers]
Debt-free, Rs1.09 lakh cr net worth and 1.22x CFO/PAT fund capex internally. Stock is 34% off high at 3.3x book. [Numbers]
bear: Three straight quarters of falling PAT YoY (-6.4%, -9.1%, -26.4%). TTM PAT is below FY26, so the 26.6x P/E is on shrinking earnings. [Numbers]
Margins at 8-9% are below the 10% 2030 EBIT target. The 'temporary' cost thesis has failed for two quarters. [Numbers] [Q4FY26 call]
Heavy capex (Rs35,000cr Sanand, 500k units in FY27) plus falling margins and lengthening inventory days could compress FCF and ROCE. [AR FY26] [Numbers]
questions: Why did Q2 PAT fall 26% when EBITDA fell only 6%?
What share of the OPM drop is commodities versus pricing, mix or start-up costs?
How much of 36% revenue growth is volume versus Gujarat amalgamation or pricing?
Why did inventory days rise from 23 to 31 amid 1.9 lakh pending orders?

annual_report.business: Maruti Suzuki manufactures and sells passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, and related services in India, exporting to ~120 countries. Market leader in Indian passenger vehicles and largest vehicle exporter.

annual_report.revenue_mix: Domestic-focused India sales with 47 lakh exports (FY'26) to 120 countries. Top five destinations: South Africa, Japan, Chile, Saudi Arabia, EU.
strategy: Expand capacity to 3.65M units by FY'31 via Kharkhoda, Hansalpur, Sanand
Launch BEVs, Strong Hybrids, CNG, Flex Fuel vehicles across portfolio
Increase exports targeting 50% of India's passenger vehicle share
Shift 28% of logistics to rail for costs and emissions
Strengthen premium Nexa channel for higher-margin models and segments
annual_report.outlook: Car industry to reach 6.1-6.3M units by FY'31; small cars accelerating. CNG sales target 9L units. e VITARA EV gaining traction with 5,648 Q1 sales.
annual_report.capex_plans: ₹35,000 crores investment at Sanand for 1M capacity. Targets: 2.9M by FY'27-end, 3.65M by FY'31-end.
risks: Global economic slowdown (Iran-US war impact affecting markets)
Supply constraints: 1.9L pending orders creating fulfillment pressure
Intense automotive competition pressuring market share and margins
EV adoption pace and charging infrastructure development risks
annual_report.flags: Dividend ₹140/share (highest ever) approved. SMC owns 58.53%. Suzuki Motor Gujarat amalgamated. No auditor qualifications mentioned.
